nodes.label: "Secrets: Doppler, fnox, macOS Keychain, and environment variables" — the canonical operator guide for credential management in ray-manaloto/dotfiles: what is actually wired on this Mac, the agent contract, and the add/diagnose recipes. Rewritten 2026-08-03, every count re-measured against fnox 1.32.0 with a control arm per probe.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Global `env = true` at ~/.config/fnox/config.toml line 2: all 50 declared credentials are exported into every interactive shell and inherited by every child process — Claude Code, its subagents, every MCP server they spawn, every `mise run` task.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Ray reversed the exec-only posture on 2026-08-02 deliberately. Stated requirement: "in sync and available to all terminals and ai/llm agents". This is a DECISION, not drift — do not 'fix' it back.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: All 50 secrets additionally carry an inline `env = true`. A per-secret `env` OVERRIDES the global, so flipping the global alone changes nothing here.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `fnox exec` is no longer a confinement boundary — the parent shell already has everything.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: fnox `env` has three modes. `true` (fnox default, and this host's): visible to interactive shell / `fnox export`, `fnox exec` and `fnox get`. `"exec"`: hidden from the shell, visible to exec and get. `false`: visible only to `fnox get`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Doppler — the shared authority and value of record. Project `dotfiles`; config `dev_personal` (49 secrets) serves host and devcontainer since 2026-08-03.

nodes.label: fnox — declaration, resolution and optional encrypted cache. ~/.config/fnox/config.toml; providers `keychain`, `age`, `doppler_dotfiles_dev_personal`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: macOS Keychain — machine-local bootstrap vault. Service `mde-fnox`, two accounts: `DOPPLER_TOKEN` (unlocks everything else) and `DOPPLER_RO_TOKEN` (scoped read-only, deliberately kept out of the shell).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The environment — process delivery only, never the source of truth. Injected by shell activation (all 50) or `fnox exec`.

nodes.label: The chain: Keychain -> `DOPPLER_TOKEN` -> Doppler -> fnox declaration -> process env.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The live shape, parsed with `tomllib` rather than grepped (2026-08-03): 50 secrets declared, 50 carrying inline `env = true`, 49 on provider `doppler_dotfiles_dev_personal`, 1 on `keychain` (`DOPPLER_TOKEN`), 49 `sync = { provider = "age" }` blocks, 0 occurrences of `env = "exec"`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 50 secrets carry 49 sync blocks and that is CORRECT. `AGE_PRIVATE_KEY` is the key that decrypts the age cache, so it cannot be cached in it. Do not 'fix' 49 -> 50 anywhere sync counts appear.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Parse the format; do not pattern-match it. Three greps written for the rewrite returned confident zeros — `env = true }` matched 1 of 50 (field order), `^[A-Z_]* = {` matched 0 (spacing), `grep -c 'env = true'` counted the header comment. `tomllib` answered all three in one pass.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Doppler config `dev_personal` — 49 real secrets, read by EVERYTHING: fnox on this host and the devcontainer (`initializeCommand` downloads `${DOPPLER_CONFIG:-dev_personal}`).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Doppler config `dev` — 43 secrets, read by NOTHING by default. Retained as a per-clone opt-out via a TOP-LEVEL `[env] DOPPLER_CONFIG = "dev"` in `mise.local.toml` — never a `[tasks.up]` block, which replaces the whole task.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Measured 2026-08-03: `dev` is a strict subset of `dev_personal` — 0 names in `dev` are absent from `dev_personal`, which carries 6 extra. Both report 3 more than their real count because Doppler auto-injects DOPPLER_PROJECT / DOPPLER_CONFIG / DOPPLER_ENVIRONMENT.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A credential written to `dev` reaches nothing unless a clone opts in. Declare host credentials in `dev_personal`. This still FAILS SILENTLY.

nodes.label: The devcontainer contract asserts an `--env-file`, the `doppler.env` path and `&& doppler secrets download --format docker` — but NO CONFIG at all (`python/verification/suites.toml:507-511`). A wrong `DOPPLER_CONFIG` stays green. Alignment reduced the blast radius; it did not close the gap.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` are mise ALIASES resolved in that priority order, not distinct capabilities — control-armed against `jdx/mise:src/env.rs:591` and the cached priority table. The dev/dev_personal split therefore bought no capability.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The accepted cost of alignment: `AGE_PRIVATE_KEY` never left the host under the split and now reaches the container's `--env-file`. Decided knowingly on 2026-08-03 — do not 'fix' it back without re-deciding it.

nodes.label: That venv is an EDITABLE install (`mde.pth` points at `…/macos-development-environment/src`), so which code runs depends on which branch that sibling repo has checked out. There is no pinned copy.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `which mde-py` returning rc=1 means NOTHING (control: `which fnox` rc=0) — `mde-secret-add` is a live shell function in every interactive shell from `~/.zshrc.d/50-mde-secrets.zsh` that calls `$MDE_PROJECT_DIR/.venv/bin/mde-py` by absolute path.

nodes.label: macos-development-environment#82 is CLOSED, fixed by #83, squash-merged as `716b17d` on main. The fix adds and drops declarations by invoking the `fnox` binary, writing the file directly only when it does not exist — so it CANNOT drop the `env` mode or a per-secret opt-in.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Across all 45 refs in that clone exactly 4 carry `src/mde/secrets/manage.py`; only the local `feat/secrets-crud-architecture-a` still holds the pre-fix template rewrite. Nothing detects which branch you are on — delete that branch and the risk is zero.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Do not carry the '64 pre-fix branches' figure forward. It was true when measured against a ref set holding ~40 stale remote-tracking branches; a `git fetch --prune` removed them and the count is 1. An inherited number is not a measurement — re-derive it or label it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `add_secret` / `update_secret` / `remove_secret` each run a FULL `fnox sync --provider age --global --force`, regenerating all 49 sync ciphertexts — on main and on the stale branch alike. #83 changed `bootstrap_config`, not the sync.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: fnox is exonerated: an authorized write probe rewrote all 49 values on both its scoped and bulk paths and preserved the mode and every opt-in. The defect was mde's.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: This section was wrong twice. #515 claimed the pre-fix code was on origin/main; its probe `git cat-file -e <ref>:<path>` returned rc=128 and rc=0 for the SAME ref minutes apart while three other routes agreed with each other. When two routes disagree, one is broken — usually the probe, not the world.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: #516's replacement went stale in ONE DAY because it described a fix held off by a checked-out branch and #83 then merged it. A claim about where code lives has a shelf life measured in merges — state the ref and the date, and re-derive before relying on it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The durable layer is `mise run doctor`'s `fnox-baseline` check, which re-reads the artifact every session against `doctor.toml` (`[fnox] env = true` plus the full 50-name `env_true` set). Adding or removing a secret means changing `doctor.toml` in the same reviewed diff, or the next session reports drift and someone 'fixes' it back.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The agent operating contract — hard limits, not preferences. Survives the posture reversal unchanged: with 50 credentials reachable instead of 4, the blast radius of breaking one is 12.5x larger, not smaller.

nodes.label: Even NAMES disclose architecture — summarize counts in public logs, not inventories.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The compliant presence probe: `zsh -c '[[ -v KEY_NAME ]] || exit 20; print "credential is present"'`. Reveals presence without the value.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: THE TRAP: `${FOO:+SET}${FOO:-ABSENT}` PRINTS THE VALUE when the variable is set (`SETvisible-safe-value`). `:-` and `:=` are value-emitting substitutions. It opens with the recommended construct so it reads as compliant, and on an UNSET variable it looks perfect.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: An unset-only control arm CERTIFIES NOTHING. Arm a presence probe on a variable that IS set, with a value you can afford to see.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 2026-08-02: `${DOPPLER_TOKEN:+PRESENT}${DOPPLER_TOKEN:-ABSENT}` printed PRESENT followed by the live token, which had to be rotated. Written by an agent holding and citing the rule against it. Now denied by `hook_guard`'s `secret_value_substitution`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Presence is not correctness. Correctness needs a narrow provider health check whose response contains no secret — an identity endpoint returning an account id, or a minimal request returning an expected status.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Never record token prefixes/suffixes, hashes of low-entropy secrets, auth headers, raw env dumps, or the contents of a secret-bearing config.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The nine-step procedure for adding a secret.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 1 — confirm key name, consumer, scope, rotation expectation, and that no existing credential can be reused. The config is ALWAYS `dev_personal`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 2 (HUMAN) — create or reveal the credential at the provider.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 3 — the interactive setter, NO value argument so nothing enters argv or history: `doppler secrets set 'KEY_NAME' --project dotfiles --config dev_personal --silent`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 4 (HUMAN) — type the value into the hidden prompt.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 5 — confirm with a NAMES-ONLY listing: `doppler secrets --project dotfiles --config dev_personal --only-names | grep KEY_NAME`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 6 — declare it in fnox via `fnox edit`; the declaration holds the NAME, never the value: `KEY_NAME = { provider = "doppler_dotfiles_dev_personal", value = "KEY_NAME", env = true }`. `value` is the PROVIDER'S KEY, not the secret.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 7 — optional offline cache: `fnox sync --global -p age KEY_NAME`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `--global` is NOT optional. Without it fnox targets a `fnox.toml` in the CURRENT DIRECTORY, not the config the declaration lives in. The dry-run says `to provider age (global):` only with `-g`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 8 — REQUIRED: add the name to `doctor.toml`'s `[fnox] env_true` list in the SAME reviewed diff. Under `env = true` this is the reviewed decision: the credential lands in every terminal and every agent by default.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 9 — run a narrow consumer health check; report only the non-secret result.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: NEVER `doppler secrets set KEY 'value'` (argv/history) or `echo 'value' | doppler secrets set KEY` (plaintext through the tool call).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `mde-secret-add KEY` does steps 3-7 in one command and is the sanctioned mde interface — but it churns all 49 sync ciphertexts every time, and it does NOT touch `doctor.toml` for you. Step 8 stays manual either way.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Diagnose 'the variable isn't set' in order — each step is contract-compliant (no value read or printed) and each DISCRIMINATES, so a pass genuinely rules that layer out.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 1 — `fnox config-files`. fnox merges the user root into EVERY invocation, even with an explicit `-c`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 2 — `fnox list | grep KEY_NAME`; names only, never `--values`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 3 — `zsh -c '[[ -v KEY_NAME ]] && print present || print ABSENT'`. Under `env = true` it MUST be present.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 4 — `fnox exec -- zsh -c '[[ -v KEY_NAME ]] …'`: does it resolve to a process at all?
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Step 5 — `fnox sync --dry-run -p age KEY_NAME`: is the offline age copy stale vs Doppler? A dry-run reveals no values.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Reading the result: ABSENT in the shell but present under `fnox exec` is A REAL FAULT under `env = true` — nothing should be exec-only. Do not dismiss it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `fnox check` is NOT step 1, because for a LOST declaration it can only pass. Measured both arms on a throwaway fixture: two probe keys declared -> rc=0, 52 secrets, healthy; one declaration DELETED -> rc=0, 51 secrets, healthy. Identical verdict. `check` validates what is DECLARED; a line that vanished is not 'missing', it is unknown.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Bare `fnox check` also passes for a declared secret that does not RESOLVE. `-a` reports OK-with-warnings and names it; `--if-missing error` returns rc=1. So `--if-missing error` is the arm that can fail — use it when you want `check` to mean anything. Neither form sees a DELETED declaration.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Suspect order 1 — a HUNG `doppler` CLI. fnox's doppler provider SHELLS OUT to it, so any uncached doppler-primary secret resolves through a child `doppler` process, and a keychain authorization dialog blocks that child forever from a non-GUI process. Resolved on this host by deleting the `doppler-cli` and `gh:github.com` keychain entries.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A hang is NOT evidence of a locked keychain. `security show-keychain-info` prompts unconditionally, so ITS hang proves nothing — believing it cost ~2 hours on 2026-08-02. fnox reads a keychain secret in 0.03s, which a locked keychain cannot do.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Suspect order 2 — a stale `MISE_ENV_CACHE` entry. It can serve a dead name in ONE DIRECTORY long after the config is byte-identically restored, and grep cannot see it: the cache is encrypted. Clear ~/.local/state/mise/env-cache.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Always control-arm the negative. An ABSENT result is worthless until the same command shape returns present for something you KNOW is set: `zsh -c '[[ -v HOME ]] && print "control ok"'`. A 2026-07-29 session reported a variable 'set, 43 chars' and later 'unset' from two probes in the same session; the control arm settled it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 2026-07-29 — an agent breached the contract three ways while diagnosing a missing credential: ran `fnox get` and `doppler secrets get` to sha256-compare values; interpolated a live key into `curl -H "Authorization: $K"`; and reached for `env | grep`. Avoidable — `fnox sync --dry-run -p age` answers staleness and `[[ -v ]]` answers presence, both on the MAY list.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A silently-empty credential is the default failure mode. `${VAR:-}` interpolation in an MCP/plugin config yields an EMPTY STRING for any credential that is absent, misnamed or unset. The server starts, reports healthy, and degrades to an anonymous tier. Check the consumer's AUTHENTICATED IDENTITY, never its connection status.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A running process keeps its env snapshot. After a rotation, restart consumers — a green write proves nothing about live processes.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `fnox sync` caches; a Doppler change does not propagate to the encrypted cache until you re-sync.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `-c` ADDS a config, it does not isolate one. fnox merges ~/.config/fnox/config.toml into every invocation. A test that forgets this reaches live user state — that is how a mutation test wiped this host's config on 2026-08-01.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The often-quoted "1.7s -> 2.7s" shell-startup cost is an INHERITED figure the rewrite could not reproduce: three consecutive `zsh -ic true` runs measured 0.99s / 1.33s / 3.12s (control `zsh -f`: 0.058s). Same-input variance is LARGER than the claimed 1s delta — the direction is real, the magnitude is not established.

nodes.label: mise masks digits in `mise run` output when a redacted value is short and all-digit — `[redacted][redacted]3` for 113. Read numbers from a recorded `rc=` or a non-mise invocation.

nodes.label: "Evidence — secrets-out-of-the-shell-env" — the measurement annex behind the dotfiles repo's `.claude/rules/secrets-out-of-the-shell-env.md` eager rule. It holds the 2026-07-27 __MISE_DIFF exposure incident, the scanner/fix/verification probe tables, the 2026-07-30 wipe incident and its full root-cause investigation (fnox exonerated, mde-py's bootstrap_config + full resync identified as the actual mechanism, mde-secret-add identified as the sanctioned-interface trigger), the 2026-08-02-g `:-` fallback leak, the 2026-08-02 posture reversal to `env = true`, and exec-era sections preserved verbatim from a since-rewritten guide.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: On 2026-07-27, `fnox activate` exported 49 variables into the login shell; mise records the whole environment delta in `__MISE_DIFF` (zlib-compressed, base64-encoded, inherited by every child process) so it can undo it on directory exit. Decoded, the live blob carried an AWS access key id and secret, several API tokens, an app password, and a Google client secret. This is the incident behind the `secrets-out-of-the-shell-env` rule.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Control-armed probe: pickaxing the exact live 2026-07-27 credential values across the FULL git history of both public repos (dotfiles and knowledge-base) returned 0 commits in each, against a control term that returned 339 hits (dotfiles) and 94 hits (knowledge-base) — so the probe discriminates and the zero is a real negative, not a blind probe. Conclusion: nothing from the __MISE_DIFF exposure reached a public remote. The exposure was still real: the blob sat in every child process, and one `env > notes.md` inside a tracked directory would have published all of it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The single `AKIA`-prefixed string found anywhere in dotfiles' git history is a vendor example string inside `docs/research/mintlify-cache/`, not a real AWS access key id — distinguishing a pattern match from an actual leaked credential.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Measured 2026-07-27 with synthetic, format-valid credentials in two forms of the same content: gitleaks 8.30.1 found 2 leaks in a plaintext env dump but 0 in the same content encoded as a `__MISE_DIFF` blob (zlib-compressed, base64-encoded); betterleaks 1.7.1 found 1 leak in plaintext and 0 in the blob form. The control arm (the plaintext case) fires for both scanners, so the zero on the compressed form is a real negative, not a blind probe: both scanners are pattern matchers and compression destroys the patterns they match on. This is the one gap that justifies writing custom decode code for this threat at all — and the custom code covers only the decode step.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The fix was probed on the pinned fnox 1.31.1 in a throwaway project, both arms armed: with `env = "exec"` set, `fnox export --format shell` emitted ONLY the variables carrying the per-secret `env = true` opt-in, while `fnox exec -- env` still carried both the opted-in and the exec-only variables. The rule's behavior table is this tool's measured behavior, not a restatement of its release notes.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Finding: a local override is NOT honoured at the fnox user config root (`~/.config/fnox/config.toml`) — `fnox config-files` lists it alone, and adding `config.local.toml` or `fnox.local.toml` beside it changed that output not at all. Control arm: in a PROJECT directory the same command lists `fnox.toml` AND `fnox.local.toml` AND the user root — three lines — so the command CAN report more than one file; the override layer is scoped to project directories only, not the user root.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Finding: the fnox user config file is GENERATED — its first line reads "Managed by `mde-py secrets bootstrap-config`. Do not edit by hand." — so a hand edit survives only until the next bootstrap run. The durable fix belongs in mde-py's generator, not in the file itself.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Finding: two variables must be opted back in with per-secret `env = true`, and they are the two this repo actually runs on: `.mcp.json` interpolates one at MCP-server spawn, and `gh` — used by ship/land/automerge and every `gh api` call — reports its active account as the environment-authenticated one, with a narrower-scoped fallback behind it. Making those two exec-only would degrade tooling silently rather than loudly.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A grep of `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.config/mise/config.toml`, `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.gitconfig` and `home/**` for all 49 secret names found ZERO other declared consumers. Control arm: the same grep for `export|source|eval` in `.zshrc` returned 7 hits, so the grep mechanism itself works. Stated bound: this only finds DECLARED consumers in config files — a tool that reads a variable by convention (not declared anywhere) would show zero here too, so absence in this probe is not absence of a real consumer.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: APPLIED 2026-07-27, by Ray, not by an agent: the standing rule against touching a user-level file unasked was honoured by having Ray run the prepared recipe himself. 46 of the 49 credentials went exec-only; 3 were opted back in with per-secret `env = true`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Even though Ray had explicitly approved this one user-level-file edit, the harness's own permission layer still refused the write — correctly, and independently of Ray's approval. Two layers exist (the standing-rule check and the harness permission system), and the outer one does not read approvals granted at the inner layer, which is why the edit had to be prepared here and executed by Ray directly.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The fix was verified in a FRESH interactive login shell, not the session's own: the opted-in variable was set, the two exec-only ones were not, and the recorded `__MISE_DIFF` delta shrank from roughly 16.8 KB decoded to a 5.2 KB blob.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The first attempt at that verification was broken and looked like a clean pass: `zsh -l -c` is NON-interactive and never sources `.zshrc`, so nothing activated and the variable read as "absent" for the wrong reason. It was only caught because the control arm — running the same probe against the pre-fix config — ALSO said "absent", which should have been impossible if the probe were real. `-i` (interactive mode) is what makes the probe able to answer the question at all.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: mise redacts every occurrence of a redacted variable's VALUE in `mise run` task output. fnox marks all of its variables redacted by default, and two of them hold one-character, all-digit values: `GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` and `GEMINI_TELEMETRY_LOG_PROMPTS`. So mise faithfully masks every occurrence of that single digit anywhere in every `mise run` output line — meaning a NUMBER read from `mise run` output cannot be trusted. `LANGSMITH_WORKSPACE_ID` is worse: it holds an EMPTY value. These are telemetry flags, not secrets; the digit-masking was never a mise bug, it is collateral damage from treating a non-secret as a secret.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` — a fnox-managed variable holding a one-character, all-digit value, marked redacted by fnox's default, which causes mise to mask that digit everywhere it appears in `mise run` output.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `GEMINI_TELEMETRY_LOG_PROMPTS` — a fnox-managed variable holding a one-character, all-digit value, marked redacted by fnox's default, causing the same digit-masking collateral damage as `GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `LANGSMITH_WORKSPACE_ID` — a fnox-managed variable that holds an EMPTY value while still being marked redacted.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The 2026-08-02 posture reversal: Ray reversed the exec-only posture and put ALL 49 credentials back under `env = true`, available in every terminal and to every agent again. This put the digit-masking condition back, since it depends only on a variable being both redacted and shell-exported, not specifically on the `mde-py` re-bootstrap path an earlier prediction had named.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Re-measured 2026-08-03 with a control arm, after the posture reversal put digit-masking back: `mise run p2996-hash` printed `0748f3[redacted]46e984492` (25 characters, one digit masked), while the CONTROL — the identical underlying command run via `uv run --project python dotfiles-setup p2996-hash`, bypassing mise — printed `0748f3146e984492` (16 characters, rc=0). Same prefix, same suffix; `mise run` had replaced exactly one character with the redaction marker. Lesson: read every number from a non-`mise` invocation or a recorded `rc=`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A prior prediction — "[digit-masking] returns if `mde-py` re-bootstraps the config" — named the wrong trigger. A POLICY REVERSAL (the 2026-08-02 posture change) fired instead, not a re-bootstrap; the re-bootstrap failure mode it named is now fixed at source by mde issue #82's PR. Lesson: a hedge that names one cause is not coverage of the whole class of causes.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Operational finding about CREATING a keychain item for fnox (moved out of the eager rule 2026-08-03, since it is trivia about creation rather than about the exposure hazard): grant the reader on the ACL with `security add-generic-password -T <real binary>` — fnox's own binary path is version-pinned, so the grant breaks on upgrade. And `security ... -w` returns HEX for a multi-line value: `AGE_PRIVATE_KEY` came back as 377 bytes of hex versus 188 bytes decoded, so consumers must hex-decode it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The wipe RECURRED on 2026-07-30, the same day the #418 project-doctor check shipped. `~/.config/fnox/config.toml` was rewritten at 00:47 local (CDT), which wiped both the global `env = "exec"` line and all 4 per-secret `env = true` opt-ins. For roughly 4h40m, all 49 credentials were shell-visible again, inherited by every child process — the exact exposure the rule exists to prevent. The wiped file is preserved at `~/.config/fnox/config.toml.WIPED-evidence-20260730-055104` (that suffix is UTC; the file dates from 00:51:04 local).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 20:07 (Jul 29, local CDT): `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` was opted back in as the 4th per-secret `env = true` entry. Verified immediately: `fnox export` named 4 of 49 as exported.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: ~20:10 (Jul 29, local CDT): `mise run doctor`'s `fnox-baseline` check ran and reported PASS, confirming the state after the 4th opt-in.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:47 local CDT (Jul 30): `~/.config/fnox/config.toml` was rewritten. The global `env = "exec"` line was GONE, and all 4 per-secret `env = true` entries were GONE — this is the wipe event itself.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:48 local CDT (Jul 30): `mise run doctor`'s `fnox-baseline` check reported DRIFT — its first real firing, catching the wipe one minute after it happened.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:50 local CDT (Jul 30): the config was restored. `fnox export` was back to naming 4 of 49 exported, and `mise run doctor` reported 7/7 checks passing.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Lesson: read the clock before reading the timeline. The FIRST write-up of the 2026-07-30 wipe incident mixed local and UTC timestamps in one table, which made the wipe read as having happened "last night" when it had actually happened only 30 minutes before the write-up. `date -u`-derived filenames (like the WIPED-evidence suffix) and locally-observed mtimes must not appear in the same column unlabelled.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Diffing the pre-wipe backup, the WIPED file, and the restored file with a TOML parser (comparing keys and value LENGTHS only, never values — `scratchpad/fnox_structdiff.py`) showed: global `env` was `"exec"` pre-wipe, ABSENT in WIPED, `"exec"` again restored; per-secret `env = true` count was 3 pre-wipe (pre-CONTEXT7 opt-in), 0 in WIPED, 4 restored; secrets/providers count stayed 49/3 throughout; the `sync.value` ciphertexts for ALL 49 secrets were REPLACED in the WIPED file (net +436 characters) and stayed unchanged from WIPED in the restored file; the outer `value`/`provider` fields were unchanged throughout.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: This structdiff finding OVERTURNS the first write-up's correction #1, which claimed "all 49 sync blocks survived" the wipe. That is true only STRUCTURALLY — every ciphertext inside all 49 sync blocks was actually regenerated. The wipe event was therefore a WHOLE-CONFIG REBUILD PLUS A FULL RE-SYNC, not a surgical removal of just the `env` fields. A signature read at the wrong granularity (block presence, not ciphertext identity) looked like a half-match when it was actually a full rebuild.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `grep -c 'env = true'` is NOT a control arm for "how many opt-ins are there": it counted 5 where the TOML parser (fnox_structdiff.py) correctly counted 4, because the config file's own header COMMENT contains the literal string "env = true" as prose. Lesson: parse the format, don't pattern-match it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The recorded hypothesis after the wipe was that fnox ITSELF drops the `env` field when it re-serialises the config file. Ray authorized a real write against the LIVE credential store to test it — a `--dry-run` could not settle the question, because the suspected defect lived specifically in the write path. The test was backed up first and restored byte-exact after; it read and compared names, never values.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Probe: `fnox activate zsh` — did NOT write to the config file at all.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Probe: `fnox hook-env -s zsh` (the shell precmd hook fnox installs) — did NOT write to the config file; its output hash was byte-identical across runs, and it correctly exported an opted-in variable.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Probe: `fnox sync -g -p age <ONE_SECRET> -f` — DID write, regenerating 1 of 49 ciphertexts, and the `env` field was PRESERVED — both the global `env` mode and all 4 per-secret opt-ins survived.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Probe: `fnox sync -g -p age -f` (all secrets) — DID write, regenerating all 49/49 ciphertexts and reproducing the wipe's EXACT ciphertext-replacement signature, yet the `env` field was PRESERVED — both the global mode and all 4 opt-ins survived. This bulk arm is what makes the exoneration a real negative: it rewrote every one of the 49 values, so it COULD have dropped the `env` fields, and did not.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Conclusion: fnox is EXONERATED. fnox round-trips the `env` field correctly on both its scoped (`fnox sync -g -p age <ONE>`) and its bulk (`fnox sync -g -p age`, all secrets) write paths — the earlier hypothesis that fnox itself drops `env` on re-serialisation was falsified by an armed probe, not by assumption. Bonus: `fnox activate` is control-armed for free by any agent session, since the Bash tool sources `~/.zshrc` on every call (that is where the `fnox` shell function comes from), and the config's mtime does not move across dozens of such calls.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `macos-development-environment/src/mde/secrets/manage.py` — the file identified as the actual author of the wipe, in the sibling `macos-development-environment` (mde-py) repo. Line references in this analysis were RE-DERIVED, not inherited from an earlier pass.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `bootstrap_config()` at manage.py:247 rebuilds the fnox config file from scratch as a list of literal lines. It emits each secret as `KEY = { provider, value }` (L318) and preserves ONLY `DOPPLER_TOKEN` specially (L292-296). It never reads or re-emits the `env` field at all, so both the global `env = "exec"` mode and every per-secret `env = true` opt-in are DROPPED BY CONSTRUCTION — not by a bug, by what the function was written to do. The "Do not edit by hand" header comment is written at L275. `bootstrap_config` writes NO `sync` blocks at all, so bootstrap alone cannot by itself produce the wiped file, which still had all 49 sync blocks.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `add_secret` at manage.py:166 calls `bootstrap_config()` and then immediately runs a FULL `_run_fnox_sync_age()` (L169), which regenerates all 49 sync blocks with fresh ciphertexts. `update_secret` (L177) is a plain alias for `add_secret`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `remove_secret` at manage.py:208 calls `bootstrap_config()` and then immediately runs a full `_run_fnox_sync_age()` (L211), regenerating all 49 sync blocks with fresh ciphertexts — the same composite behavior as `add_secret`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `bootstrap_config()` (drops `env` by construction) followed by a full `_run_fnox_sync_age()` (regenerates all 49 ciphertexts) reproduces the observed wipe signature EXACTLY, and neither half does so on its own — bootstrap alone leaves no sync blocks at all, and a bare resync alone would preserve `env`. The composite call chain inside `add_secret`/`update_secret`/`remove_secret` is the actual mechanism.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The invoker of the 2026-07-30 wipe was `mde-secret-add`, run BY HAND — the DOCUMENTED HAPPY PATH for adding a secret. A first investigative pass had reported the invoker as "non-interactive and unlogged"; that report was FALSE, and the fault was the probe, not the world — the command was sitting in `~/.zsh_history` the entire time.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:45:36 (CDT): Ray asks an agent, in a codex session, "i have a linear key how do i set it?"
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:46:11 (CDT): the agent, reading the mde repo's own documentation, answers "run `mde-secret-add LINEAR_API_KEY`".
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:46:51 (CDT): Ray runs `source ~/.zshrc` then `mde-secret-add LINEAR_API_KEY` — recorded as ONE multi-line zsh history entry — per `~/.zsh_history`. This is the exact command that triggers the wipe mechanism (`add_secret` → `bootstrap_config()` + full resync).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:47:00 (CDT): the config file was rewritten by the `mde-secret-add LINEAR_API_KEY` invocation — mode and all 4 opt-ins gone, all 49 ciphertexts fresh. This matches the wipe timeline's 00:47 entry.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 00:47:19 (CDT): Ray confirms, in the codex session, "it is set" — LINEAR_API_KEY was successfully added, but as a side effect the wipe had already occurred.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `add_secret` is an UPSERT, and `LINEAR_API_KEY` already existed in the config — which is why the total key count stayed at 49 through the wipe, and why "this was an update of an existing key" could be deduced from the artifact alone, before the actual command was found.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: A MULTI-LINE zsh history entry defeated a single-line parser, and the resulting absence was reported as a finding. zsh writes a history entry as `: <epoch>:<elapsed>;` followed by a body that may span multiple lines (continuations end with a backslash). The parser used was the regex `^: (\d+):(\d+);(.*)$`, applied per line, so it captured only `source ~/.zshrc` and SILENTLY DROPPED the `mde-secret-add` command that followed on the next line. The fix is to split on the entry MARKER and take everything up to the next marker, not to parse line-by-line.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The control arm that ran during the invoker investigation tested the WRONG property: it confirmed that `sharehistory` was enabled — i.e. that the history FILE was complete — which was true and irrelevant, because the broken component was the READER (the single-line regex), not the file. Lesson: arm the step you actually depend on. The cheap catch here would have been grepping the corpus for a token known to be present (`mde-secret` → 2 hits, ever) instead of trusting a structured parse.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Ruled out as the wipe's cause: launchd. 8 user LaunchAgents plists were checked, and NONE match mde/fnox/secret/doppler BY CONTENT; 7 do match on the `Label` field, which is what proves the grep can actually see plist content. The mde maintenance/validation agents referenced by some labels are not even installed. The first investigative pass had only grepped LABELS with `head -5`, a bounded probe that missed this.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Ruled out as the wipe's cause: any Claude session. ZERO tool calls occurred between 00:44 and 00:49 across 2,272 transcripts spanning 70 projects on the machine; the dotfiles project's own session was specifically idle from 00:43:44 to 00:48:19, bracketing the wipe.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Ruled out as the wipe's cause: a Claude Code hook (which would be invisible to session transcripts). No settings file anywhere invokes `mde-py`; `.claude/settings.json` matches the string `hooks` only 6 times, none of them an mde-py call.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Ruled out as the wipe's cause: a mise `enter` hook. There is NO `[hooks]` section in any mde-related mise config — this was the LEADING hypothesis at one point, and it was killed by actually READING the config rather than by probing behavior.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Ruled out as a route to an answer (not ruled out as a cause, but as a source of evidence): mde-py's own logging. There is no `bootstrap_config_written` log entry anywhere, and mde's logs have been stale since APRIL — so this route could never have answered the question regardless of what happened.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Doppler's audit log is INCONCLUSIVE about the wipe, not negative evidence: `doppler activity` returns empty because the token in use lacks workspace scope, while `doppler secrets --only-names` (a different, narrower-scoped call) does return rows. This is a "never asked" result, not a "no" — the audit-log check never actually ran with sufficient permission to answer.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Why the wipe bug is severe rather than a one-off: `mde-secret-add`/`-update`/`-rm` are the SANCTIONED interface for managing secrets — an agent reading the mde repo's own docs recommends them unprompted, which is exactly what happened in this incident. So EVERY secret added or updated re-exposes all 49 credentials to the shell, until something re-reads the config.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The wipe bug, with its confirmed trigger (the `mde-secret-add` happy path calling `bootstrap_config()` + full resync), was filed as macos-development-environment issue #82. Status as of 2026-08-03: CLOSED, fixed by PR #83 (merged as 716b17d) — `bootstrap_config()` now reconciles through fnox itself, so there is no longer a hand-written template that can drop the `env` field.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: knowledge-base issue #74 was the sibling tracking issue on this repo's own side, and was the ONLY record of this repo's own awareness of the mde-py wipe defect. It was CLOSED 2026-08-03 with an evidence comment; the issue had also carried a "prefer `fnox exec --`" recommendation that turned out to be the INVERSE of the posture that was actually chosen (the 2026-08-02 reversal to `env = true`).

nodes.label: Durable lesson 1: "APPLIED 2026-07-27 by Ray" was recorded as settled, and nothing re-read the config artifact for three days — until the wipe recurred. A config whose generator you do not own is not fixed by editing it once; it is fixed by a CHECK that re-reads it continuously, which is what `fnox-baseline` (in `doctor.toml`) is.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Durable lesson 2: an untested hypothesis, left in place, quietly becomes the working story. The investigation blamed fnox itself for the wipe, on plausibility alone, for roughly a day — one authorized write-based probe settled the question in two commands.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Durable lesson 3: "I could not find it" is not "it is not there." Publishing an absence as an attribution (the first pass's "non-interactive and unlogged") dressed a failed search as a conclusion. An unattributed cause is an open question and should be labelled as one until a SOURCE — not a silence — closes it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The `:-` fallback leak, 2026-08-02-g: the same rule's second breach on the same day. Rule 7 had been written earlier that day, after a `${(P)k}` expansion printed four live credentials. Hours later, an agent holding that rule and actively citing it ran `printf "%s" "${DOPPLER_TOKEN:+PRESENT}${DOPPLER_TOKEN:-ABSENT}"`, which printed `PRESENT` followed by the LIVE `dp.ct.`-prefixed Doppler CLI token to the terminal. The token had to be rotated afterward.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Why the leaking command passed review at a glance: `${VAR:+PRESENT}` is the exact form the rule RECOMMENDS, and the construct opens with it, so it reads as compliant. The leak is in the second half: `${VAR:-ABSENT}` is a VALUE-EMITTING substitution — for a variable that IS set, it expands to the variable's VALUE, not to the fallback text "ABSENT".
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Reproduced on a harmless value (`FOO=visible-safe-value`): `${FOO:+SET}` → `SET`; `[ -n "$FOO" ] && echo SET || echo ABSENT` → `SET`; the dangerous combined form `${FOO:+SET}${FOO:-ABSENT}` → `SETvisible-safe-value` (the value leaks); `${NOPE_UNSET:+SET}${NOPE_UNSET:-ABSENT}` on an UNSET variable → `ABSENT` (looks perfectly safe). The last row is the whole trap: on an unset variable, the bad form looks exactly like the safe presence-check pattern.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Correction forced into the rule, #1: the claim "the exposed set is exactly the four `env = true` opt-ins, knowable in advance" was FALSE. `DOPPLER_TOKEN` is exec-only, measured in the SAME command as `PRESENT` under `fnox exec` and `ABSENT` in a plain shell — and it still leaked, because the leaking probe had wrapped ITSELF in `fnox exec`. Any of the full 49 secrets is printable by a probe that wraps itself in `fnox exec`; only an UNWRAPPED probe is capped at the four opt-ins.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Correction forced into the rule, #2: the leaking probe DID carry a control arm — a nonexistent variable, which correctly returned `ABSENT`. But that control only exercises the `:-` branch on an UNSET variable, which is the SINGLE case where it cannot leak. This is `probes-need-a-control-arm.md` rule 8: a fixture that could not have produced the other outcome is not a real control. Lesson: arm a PRESENCE probe, on a variable that IS set with a value you can afford to see, before pointing the pattern at a real secret.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Incidental finding, discovered because the leaking probe was checking whether a Doppler token already existed before ticket #487 would provision one: it does exist. `DOPPLER_TOKEN` lives in the macOS keychain via fnox, declared by mde's `bootstrap_config` (manage.py:296) as a DECLARATION ONLY. `doppler me` reports the CLI authenticated as `type: cli`, name `dotfiles-20260327` — a PERSONAL CLI login, and the `dp.ct.` prefix confirms `DOPPLER_TOKEN` is that same class of credential. So ticket #487's premise ("provision a token") was wrong: one already exists, and it is the OPPOSITE of scoped/read-only/expiring.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The `env` mode access-control table, as the guide documented it (added 2026-07-29): `env = true` (fnox's own default) is exported to the interactive shell/`fnox export`, `fnox exec`, AND `fnox get`. `env = "exec"` (this repo's chosen posture at the time) is NOT exported to the interactive shell/`fnox export`, but IS available to `fnox exec` and `fnox get`. `env = false` is not available to the shell OR `fnox exec`, only to `fnox get`. A secret being declared and resolvable does NOT by itself mean it reaches the shell — that depends entirely on this per-secret/global `env` setting.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Under the exec-only posture, four secrets carried an explicit per-secret `env = true` opt-in: `CONTEXT7_API_KEY`, `EXA_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN` — chosen because each of their consumers can ONLY read the process environment, not a keychain or a config file.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` — opted back in to `env = true` because the Upstash context7 MCP plugin interpolates `"Authorization": "${CONTEXT7_API_KEY:-}"` directly from the process environment when it spawns; there is no other place the plugin can read it from.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `EXA_API_KEY` — opted back in to `env = true` because the `/last30days` engine's web lane reads it from the PROCESS ENVIRONMENT; it lives in neither that plugin's own `.env` file nor the keychain.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `EXA_API_KEY`'s RECORDED reason for needing `env = true` went stale: it originally read "an `.mcp.json` `${VAR}` interpolation at MCP-server spawn", which stopped being true on 2026-07-30 when this repo's `.mcp.json` was emptied out — but the credential was STILL required, by a second consumer (the last30days web lane) that had never been written down anywhere. Lesson: a stated reason that names only one consumer is an implicit claim that there is only one, and that claim nearly let a live credential's exec-only opt-in get dropped as "no longer needed".
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `GITHUB_TOKEN` — opted back in to `env = true` because `gh` reports its ACTIVE account as the environment-authenticated one (with a narrower-scoped fallback behind it), and this repo's `ship`/`land`/`automerge` tasks and every `gh api` call depend on `gh`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN` — opted back in to `env = true` because mise rate-limits GitHub API calls to 60 requests/hour without it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: An internal inconsistency in the (now-superseded) guide: its line 90 stated 3 per-secret opt-ins while its line 43 stated 4. This was never reconciled at the time — the true count was 3 on 2026-07-27 and became 4 starting 2026-07-29 (when `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` was added as the 4th).
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The generator's emitted field set, measured against the live config — the sharpest statement of the #82 defect: at the time measured, the config held global `env = "exec"` (1 instance), 3 per-secret `env = true` entries, and 49 `sync = { provider = "age", ... }` blocks. `bootstrap_config()` EMITS zero of all three categories. So a single `bootstrap-config` run silently reverts every secret to shell-exported, undoing the entire reason `env = "exec"` was adopted.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: 2026-07-29: the Context7 MCP server ran ANONYMOUS for days, and nothing noticed. The Upstash context7 plugin interpolates `"Authorization": "${CONTEXT7_API_KEY:-}"`; since that secret was exec-only at the time, the header resolved to EMPTY, and the server silently used the anonymous tier — while still reporting `✓ connected` the whole time. This produced rule 5's "check the consumer's authenticated identity, never its connection status."
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: What made the context7-anonymous incident invisible: `${VAR:-}` substitutes an empty string instead of failing outright — silent by construction. Doppler-to-fnox sync was perfectly healthy the whole time (`fnox check` green, value matched Doppler exactly), so every instinct to blame "the sync" was wrong; the actual break was downstream, in the shell-export gate. The opt-in list itself was drawn BEFORE the consumer existed: the three `env = true` entries were chosen 2026-07-27 for the three consumers that existed then, and the context7 plugin arrived 2026-07-29 with nothing re-checking the list against it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Generalisation from the context7-anonymous incident: a NEW env-var consumer is a new opt-in decision, and nothing enforces that decision gets made. Tracked as dotfiles issue #418 — a project-doctor SessionStart check verifying that every `${VAR}` interpolated by an MCP/plugin config carries `env = true`.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Under `env = true` (the current posture), the exec-only MECHANISM behind the context7-anonymous incident is gone — nothing is exec-only, so no interpolation resolves empty for THAT reason. But the FAILURE SHAPE is not gone: any credential that is absent, misnamed, or genuinely unset still yields an empty string through `${VAR:-}`, and the consumer still degrades quietly rather than failing loudly.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: Eventual intent, stated by Ray on 2026-07-20: migrate the fnox/mde integration into a Claude Code skill, with the dotfiles repo managing the macOS environment directly. As of this document, neither step is done, so the current guide remains only the interim contract.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: On the machine this was measured on, fnox is shell-activated: 3 `FNOX_*` variables are present in a live process, and `DOPPLER_TOKEN` resolves correctly from the keychain — meaning no bootstrap step is needed on this particular host.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: An `age` encryption provider is configured, with `recipients = ["age16djrq…"]`, which is what makes the encrypted-cache sync path (`fnox sync`) available at all in this setup.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: The exec-only era ran from 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-02, when Ray reversed the posture: all 49 credentials became `env = true` again, available in every terminal and to every agent. The section documenting the exec-only mode's adoption was kept verbatim (not deleted) because the MECHANISMS it documents are still live — `bootstrap_config()` still regenerates the config the same way, and the fnox env-mode table still describes how the tool behaves — only the CHOSEN default changed.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: One thing inverts usefully under the posture reversal: fnox's own DEFAULT `env` value is `true`, and `bootstrap_config()` emits only `provider` + `value` (never `env`) — so under the NEW posture, a bootstrap regeneration now lands on the DESIRED state by accident, rather than the wrong one. The wipe class that used to eat `env = "exec"` and its four opt-ins is now BENIGN for the mode itself; what remains fragile is any newly ADDED per-secret declaration and the `sync` ciphertext blocks, which still get regenerated on every bootstrap+resync.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: fnox v1.30.0, released 2026-07-09, added the exec-only `env` mode. Its own release notes name this exact threat class explicitly: it keeps secrets out of the interactive shell "where AI coding agents and other inherited processes would see them," while still injecting them into `fnox exec` subprocesses. The fnox version measured throughout this document is 1.31.1, so the feature was available for all of it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: With `env = "exec"` set, there is no environment DELTA for mise to record in the first place, so `__MISE_DIFF` stops carrying credentials at the source — this is the mechanism that actually closes the original 2026-07-27 exposure vector, and everything else in this document is the net underneath it, not a substitute for it.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: fnox — the secrets-management CLI this document evaluates. It provides per-secret and global `env` mode control (`true`/`"exec"`/`false`), `fnox export`, `fnox exec`, `fnox get`, `fnox sync`, `fnox activate`, `fnox hook-env`, and `fnox config-files`. Version 1.31.1 is the pinned version measured throughout this document; v1.30.0 (2026-07-09) is where the exec-only `env` mode shipped.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `__MISE_DIFF` — a mise-internal environment variable that records the WHOLE environment delta caused by directory-scoped activation (zlib-compressed, base64-encoded), so mise can undo the delta on directory exit. It is inherited by every child process, which is what made the 2026-07-27 `fnox activate` export of 49 credentials into it a real exposure even though nothing reached a public git remote.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)

nodes.label: `fnox-baseline` — the `doctor.toml` check that re-reads the live fnox config every session and reports DRIFT if the expected `env` mode/opt-in state does not match. It is what actually catches a wipe when one recurs (it caught the 2026-07-30 wipe one minute after it happened), which is the durable fix for a config file this repo does not own the generator of.
nodes.author: Raymond Manaloto (ray-manaloto/dotfiles)
